I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to protect income, use water carefully, and match the weather and soils I know well. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will finish managing that crop through harvest, then I will plant summer maize right after. I will not spread myself across many crops, because I have primary schooling, I want simple fieldwork I understand well, and I trust the crops I have grown before. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and control disease and aphids only when needed. After wheat harvest, I will keep the stubble and go quickly into summer maize with hybrid seed, lighter tillage, enough nitrogen for strong growth, and a couple of irrigations depending on rainfall. My goal is steady yield and lower risk, not chasing the highest output with complicated management.
